name: Kang-Petrov Arms KPR-74C 'Splinter'
description:
The KPR-74C is Kang-Petrov's answer to the question: what if you made the KPR-47 smaller, faster, and chambered it for a round that didn't kick like a structural complaint? The 5.56mm Combat Standard cartridge feeds through a redesigned gas system with an adjustable regulator — two positions, labeled 'Standard' and 'Adverse,' which is Kang-Petrov's engineering shorthand for 'you are in a sewer or a flood.' The receiver is stamped from recycled Slagworks industrial plate, slightly thicker than the original spec from 2031 because the recycled alloy has more inclusions than virgin steel and the engineers added margin rather than argue with purchasing. Barrel length is 415mm, giving the 5.56mm round room to develop velocity without tipping into the unwieldy. The furniture is polymer in a color Kang-Petrov calls 'Civic Grey' that every GLMZ resident calls 'the color of giving up.'

The KPR-74C is what shelf workers buy when they want something their kids can also use. The reduced recoil of the 5.56mm Combat Standard makes it genuinely accessible to smaller-framed operators, and Kang-Petrov sells a youth-length stock as a Φ12 aftermarket accessory — which tells you everything about the demographic they are courting and nothing good about it. Mid-tier buyers sometimes pick it up as a truck gun, something to keep under a delivery sled seat that does not represent a significant loss if Arcturus Civil Security decides to exercise their asset forfeiture discretion. The KPR-74C does not attract attention. That is its primary selling point.

The 74C's defining characteristic in GLMZ street culture is its interchangeability with the KPR-47 in the hands of people who do not know the difference and cannot afford to care. Fixers who work the Bridgeport corridor call it 'the Civic' with the same slightly embarrassed affection one has for a reliable but unglamorous tool. The rifles develop the same wear patterns as their larger siblings — bare metal at the charging handle, polymer furniture that cracks at the grip screw inserts and gets repaired with adhesive tape. A KPR-74C that has been properly maintained looks indistinguishable from one that has simply been used so much that everything worn has been worn smooth.
specifications:
caliber: 5.56mm Combat Standard
effective_range: 400m
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic / Full-automatic
magazine_capacity: 30 rounds
weight: 3.4 kg
tactical_use: The KPR-74C is a generalist rifle for operators who do not have the luxury of specialization. The 5.56mm Combat Standard round penetrates light armor and urban construction materials adequately without the overpenetration concerns of the 7.62mm Soviet Pattern in crowded tenement environments. The adjustable gas regulator makes it functional in GLMZ's worst environments — flooded lower-city corridors, industrial runoff zones, the particulate-heavy air of the Slagworks buffer districts. Operators who run it typically do so on semi-auto at range and switch to full-auto only for room clearance, where the lighter recoil allows for faster follow-up.
cultural_context: The KPR-74C is the rifle version of a handshake that does not mean anything. It does not signal allegiance, wealth, or affiliation — it signals that someone needed a rifle and bought the one they could afford. In GLMZ's Tier 1 and Tier 2 districts, that ubiquity is its own kind of statement: there are too many of these for any single seizure campaign to matter. Arcturus Civil Security has noted in internal briefings that KPR-74C density in the Gray Zone districts has increased 23% since the Meridian PD dissolution, which is exactly what anyone who was paying attention predicted.
story_hooks: A batch of KPR-74Cs with sequential serial numbers has appeared in three separate Excluded zone communities in the same week — someone is arming people deliberately, the numbers trace to a Slagworks warehouse that officially burned down in 2194, and the warehouse manager filed for Tier 5 residency three days ago.
The KPR-74C found at an Arcturus Civil Security checkpoint shooting has a youth-length stock installed — the ACS wants the story buried, and someone is paying well to keep it that way.
